papers.title: Evaluation of the Physical, Mechanical, Tribological, Electrochemical, and Oxidation Resistance Behaviour of Spark Plasma Sintering-Synthesized Ceramic-Reinforced Ti6Al4V-Based Composites
papers.abstract: Abstract Lightweight materials like Ti6Al4V are ideal for faster aircraft engines with higher thrust-to-mass ratios and lower fuel consumption. However, a high thrust-to-weight ratio elevates engine operating temperatures above service limits, which is detrimental to both mechanical and oxidation resistance. This study reports the synthesis of Ti6Al4V-based composites through spark plasma sintering, incorporating 5 wt.% of hexagonal boron nitride ( h -BN), titanium nitride (TiN), and aluminium nitride (AlN) nanoparticles. The synthesized composites were evaluated for microstructure, phase composition, density, microhardness, tribological properties, electrochemical behaviour, and oxidation resistance. The composites exhibit a decrease in effective density as compared to unreinforced Ti6Al4V (4.42 g/cm 3 ), with measured values of 4.12 g/cm 3 (5 h -BN/Ti6Al4V), 4.32 g/cm 3 (5TiN/Ti6Al4V), and 4.13 g/cm 3 (5AlN/Ti6Al4V), corresponding to relative densities of 97.40%, 97.63%, and 95.14%. The microhardness of unreinforced Ti6Al4V increased from 331.79 to 740.43 HV following reinforcement. Specifically, 5 h -BN/Ti6Al4V demonstrated a performance enhancement of nearly 123%, while 5TiN/Ti6Al4V and 5AlN/Ti6Al4V showed increases of 48% and approximately 52%. The unreinforced alloy demonstrates a higher mean coefficient of friction (COF) as compared to reinforced composites. 5AlN/Ti6Al4V exhibits the highest mean COF values among the composites, followed by 5TiN/Ti6Al4V, and subsequently, 5 h -BN/Ti6Al4V. Each composite exhibits a reduced specific wear rate compared with the unreinforced alloy, which can be attributed to its enhanced microhardness. 5TiN/Ti6Al4V exhibited optimal electrochemical characteristics, with a polarization resistance of 4291.6 Ω and a comparatively low corrosion rate of 0.037641 mm/year. Furthermore, 5TiN/Ti6Al4V exhibits markedly improved oxidation resistance, as indicated by its minimal weight gain of 2.06% compared to its counterparts. The synthesis of composites with enhanced performance is anticipated to expand Ti6Al4V alloy's aerospace applications and help develop more sustainable aerospace technologies.

papers.title: The effect of heat treatment on the structural and performance evolution of plasma electrolytic oxidation coatings
papers.abstract: To improve the mechanical durability of biomedical implants, this work examines how heat treatment influences the structure and properties of plasma electrolytic oxidation (PEO) coatings on Ti-6Al-4V alloy. The evolution of the coating was evaluated in terms of phase composition, surface characteristics, and fatigue performance using X-ray diffraction, microhardness tests, and residual stress analysis. It is found that heat treatment markedly improves the crystallinity and hardness of the coating, with the 800 °C treated sample reaching around 670 HV. However, the effect on fatigue life is strongly temperature dependent. A treatment at 400 °C yields the best fatigue resistance, attributed to increased coating densification (porosity reduced to ∼8%) and the preservation of residual compressive stresses, which help inhibit crack initiation. In contrast, treatments above 600 °C promote the anatase-to-rutile phase transition. This transformation introduces residual tensile stresses and encourages microcrack formation, significantly degrading fatigue life. Moreover, surface wettability evolves with phase composition and defect density: the hydrophilic rutile phase formed at 600 °C minimizes the water contact angle, whereas increased microcracking at 800 °C traps air and raises the contact angle. These findings establish heat temperature-dependent structure-property relationships critical for orthopedic coating design.

summary_zh.motivation: 改善生物医学植入物的机械耐久性，探究热处理对PEO涂层结构和性能的影响。
summary_zh.method: 在不同温度下对Ti-6Al-4V合金上的PEO涂层进行热处理，表征相组成、表面特性和疲劳性能。
summary_zh.result: 400°C热处理提高了涂层致密度和残余压应力，最佳疲劳抗力；600°C以上促进锐钛矿向金红石转变，降低疲劳寿命。
summary_zh.validation: 通过XRD、显微硬度、残余应力和疲劳实验验证了热处理温度的影响。

summary_en.motivation: To improve the mechanical durability of biomedical implants, this work investigates how heat treatment influences the structure and properties of plasma electrolytic oxidation (PEO) coatings on Ti-6Al-4V.
summary_en.method: PEO coatings on Ti-6Al-4V were heat-treated at various temperatures, and the evolution of phase composition, surface characteristics, and fatigue performance was evaluated.
summary_en.result: Heat treatment at 400°C improved coating densification and preserved residual compressive stresses, yielding the best fatigue resistance, while treatments above 600°C induced anatase-to-rutile transformation and microcracks, degrading fatigue life.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed using X-ray diffraction, microhardness tests, residual stress analysis, and fatigue experiments.

papers.title: Surface modification of Ti-13Nb-13Zr implant alloy by ZrO2 nano-particles coating using RF plasma magnetron sputtering
papers.abstract: • ZrO2 Coating on Ti-13Nb-13Zr Alloy: The use of RF plasma magnetron sputtering technique to enhance the chemical and biological properties of Ti-13Nb-13Zr alloy surface. • Optimal RF Power Determination: The optimal power of 150 W for ZrO2 coating was found to provide the highest coating thickness and best corrosion resistance properties. • High Corrosion Resistance: The corrosion rate for the 150 W coated sample was reduced to 0.169×10⁻³ mm per year, nearly 20 times lower than the uncoated sample. • Hydroxyapatite (HA) Formation: After immersion in SBF solution for 30 days, the highest amount of hydroxyapatite (HA) formation was observed on the 150 W coated sample, indicating superior osseointegration potential. The most wildly clinically used Ti-6Al-4V (Ti6-4) is now being replaced by a more suitable Ti-13Zr-13Nb (Ti13-13) because of its many superiorities. However, in spite of its remarkable mechanical, chemical, and biological advantages, its surface should still be coated by a suitable material in order to modify the chemical and biological characteristics. In the present work, the surface of Ti13-13 alloy was coated with a functionally graded ZrO 2 nanoparticles using RF plasma magnetron sputtering (RF-PMS) in an attempt to further enhance its chemical and biological characteristics. The samples were coated at RF plasma powers of P =100-175 W with an increasing increment of Δ P = 25 W. The phase analysis, microstructure, and corrosion resistance of the samples were determined using XRD, SEM, OCP and EIS, respectively. The biological potential was evaluated by immersing the specimens in SBF solution for 30 days and then determining their structural and corrosion behaviors in an attempt to achieve to optimum results. The PMS of 150 W was found to be optimum in order to achieve to most suitable properties in the ZrO 2 coating

summary_en.motivation: To enhance the chemical and biological properties of Ti-13Nb-13Zr implant alloy via surface coating.
summary_en.method: ZrO2 nanoparticle coating was deposited on the alloy surface using RF plasma magnetron sputtering at different powers.
